title: Retreating into the mortal seeming
summary: A changeling choosing to become effectively mortal.

claims.text: A changeling who withdraws into the mortal seeming on purpose gains a temporary point of Banality and can no longer touch anything of the Dreaming.
If temporary Banality is above Glamour the retreat simply happens; otherwise the player rolls Willpower at a difficulty equal to current Glamour.

The changeling gets one attempt to come back alone, rolling the higher of Willpower or Glamour against current Banality; failure traps the changeling for a time set by the Mists Chart, though exposure to Glamour can free them.

title: Forgetting under Banality
summary: What happens when Banality outweighs Glamour.

claims.text: While Banality is above Glamour, a changeling risks spells of forgetting, usually starting after a story ends; one method is a daily Glamour roll against Banality on days without Glamour, with failure meaning a lapse sized by the Mists Chart.
When permanent Banality is above both permanent Glamour and Willpower, the changeling may lose the fae self for good, faster the nearer Banality is to 10.
Weekly freehold visits, one day for every point that Banality exceeds Glamour holds this off, so a changeling active among other Kithain is rarely at risk.

title: The touch of the Autumn People

claims.text: An Autumn Person needs some direct contact with a changeling, even a brief scolding, to pass on Banality.
The Storyteller rolls the Autumn Person’s Banality against the changeling’s Glamour; every success adds a point of temporary Banality.
The roll can be repeated while the changeling stays near, though Storytellers are warned not to overdo it.

title: Mortals who glimpse the Dreaming
summary: How low Banality lets humans see the fae.

claims.text: A human whose permanent Banality is under 3 notices traces of the Dreaming: chimera seem like hallucinations and Kithain give off unease or mystery.
At Banality 1 a human may see the fae as they truly are, though a Perception + Occult roll is needed to make sense of the details.
Prolonged dealings with the uncanny wear down mortal Banality, and faerie food and drink can drop it to zero, which is risky: a human in the Dreaming or Arcadia without enough Banality cannot leave.
Dauntain are kin to the fae: each had the chance to break through the Chrysalis but was denied it by trauma, sorrow and pain.
They still count as Kithain and hold some Glamour, however little.
Where Autumn People wear the Dreaming down slowly like a glacier, Dauntain strike like a blizzard, short-lived and lethal.

title: Apostates
summary: Dauntain who see Banality as the road home.

claims.text: Apostates believe the final triumph of Banality will return the fae to lost Arcadia, so the Undoing is a rebirth rather than the death of the soul.
In their view Banality balances rather than destroys, driving Glamour back to Arcadia where it belongs.
They try to convert other Kithain and kill those who refuse, aiming to wipe out every trace of Glamour on Earth.

title: Agendas
summary: The powers of Autumn Fae and Dauntain.

claims.text: Autumn Fae cannot cast cantrips and start with one level of Agendas; a Dauntain is built like a Kithain and adds three levels of Agendas to any Arts.
Freebies and experience pay for Agendas exactly as they pay for Arts.
Each Agenda names its own roll, always against the higher of the target’s Glamour or Willpower, and more successes make it last longer, up to a whole chronicle or until reversed.
Neither Autumn Fae nor Dauntain should take the Chimera or Gremayre Backgrounds.

title: Burnout
summary: An Agenda that dulls the mind and heart.

claims.text: Burnout Agendas use Empathy + Manipulation.
Mindblock stops the target thinking about one chosen topic, and Heartbind blocks one chosen positive feeling, harder against something as strong as true love.
Other effects fix the target on a dull chore, a pointless collection or a tedious new hobby; Geek Out also raises the difficulty of social rolls by 2.
